text: I've cheated plenty of times in my life, by the way. But I'm a reformed cheater. I would never do it again. Sometimes if it's going to be a one-off thing and you sleep with someone one time and then you'll never cheat again and like you don't ever talk to that person again. So that's a reformed cheater. It's not. It's a little bit different. That's acceptable? It's not acceptable, but like it's more understandable. First, do reformed cheaters exist? The answer is basically no. Maybe in one out of hundred cases or even one out of thousand, someone truly changes. But why would you play Russian roulette with your own life, your time, your mental health, on the off chance that you got that one exception? Cheating is a conscious decision, not a mistake. And once that line is crossed, it's always easier to cross it again. If someone betrayed you once, odds are they'll do it again. That's not me being harsh. That's reality. Second point, is a one-off somehow acceptable? Absolutely not. One, ten or hundred times, cheating is cheating. The number doesn't change the principle. Betrayal doesn't get graded on a curve. There's even a line often attributed to the ancient philosopher Omar Khayyam, who said, I have seen women who never cheated, and I have seen women who cheated many times, but I have never seen a woman who cheated only once. Whether he really said it or not, the wisdom is clear. Once someone cheats, it rarely ends with just one time. Bottom line, don't fool yourself with labels like reformed or one-off. Cheating is cheating, and it tells you all you need to know.
